title: Director, Regulatory and Policy - ERCOT and Western Markets
description:
About Calibrant Energy
Calibrant is a leading provider of on-site energy solutions. Calibrant develops, owns, and operates large-scale solar, battery storage, and microgrids on behalf of our customers, empowering North America's largest power users to achieve their energy goals faster, more economically, and more sustainably.
By combining innovative financing with deep industry expertise, we solve complex energy challenges for large organizations. Our performance-based, no-capex contracts ensure we only get paid when we deliver results, enabling organizations to share in cost savings without any upfront investment.
Position Overview
The Director, Regulatory and Policy – ERCOT and Western markets will lead market engagement, regulatory strategy, state policy and legislative activities focused on the Texas and Western region of the US. This includes ERCOT, WECC and CAISO markets, as well as state regulatory and policy matters within these regions. The role supports business growth by influencing policy outcomes, monitoring regulatory developments, participating in ISO/RTO stakeholder processes, and developing strategies that advance Calibrant objectives.
Key Responsibilities

- Establish regulatory and policy priorities aligned with Calibrant commercial objectives.

- Provide strategic guidance regarding legislative and regulatory developments affecting distributed energy resources, storage, and large-load customers.

- Lead engagement with ISO/RTO market committees, utilities, and stakeholders in ERCOT, WECC, CAISO regions.

- Monitor market rule developments, regulatory actions and state policy that impact Calibrant’s business and translate into actionable business guidance.

- Represent Calibrant in stakeholder meetings, industry committees, technical conferences, and trade associations.

- Advocate for ISO/RTO and state regulatory and policy outcomes that support Calibrant’s business growth, project development, and customer solutions.

- Coordinate consultants, lobbyists, and external advisors to support regulatory initiatives and strategic objectives.

- Partner with Market Development, Project Delivery, Market Operations, and Commercial teams on strategy and execution.

- Interface with utilities, transmission owners, ISOs/RTOs, and regulators to advance projects and resolve regulatory issues.

- Develop business cases, position papers, comments, and regulatory filings as needed.

- Identify regulatory risks and opportunities and communicate impacts to leadership.

- Support community, customer, and stakeholder engagement efforts related to infrastructure and energy projects.

Requirements
Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in energy policy, regulatory affairs, market strategy, or related field.

- Experience with ISO/RTO market structures and electricity industry regulatory frameworks, including experience in ERCOT and/or Western US energy markets.

- Ability to communicate complex regulatory matters to business and executive audiences in order to inform business strategy.

- Demonstrated stakeholder engagement, coalition-building, and advocacy skills.

- Experience working with utilities, ISOs/RTOs, regulators, and trade associations.

- Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

Benefits
At Calibrant Energy, our priority is to ensure that every team member feels valued and supported. We believe putting wellness first supports a full, holistic, and happier life. We support that by offering benefits that cover you and your family such as: medical, dental, vision insurances, paid time off, paid personal time, paid holidays, paid birthday, paid sick time, company paid short term disability and long term disability, company paid life insurance, 401k with a company match, and more.
Calibrant Energy is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, related medical conditions, breastfeeding or reproductive health decisions), gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, personal appearance, genetic information, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, military or veteran status, or any other category protected under applicable U.S. law.

title: Senior Business Development Director
description:
Calibrant is a leading provider of on-site energy solutions. Calibrant develops, owns, and operates large-scale solar, battery storage, linear generators, and microgrids on behalf of our customers—empowering North America's largest power users to achieve their energy goals faster, more economically, and more sustainably.
By combining innovative financing with deep industry expertise, we solve complex energy challenges for large organizations. Our performance-based, no-capex contracts ensure we only get paid when we deliver results—enabling organizations to share in cost savings without any upfront investment.
Position Overview
The Senior Business Development Director is responsible for driving Calibrant Energy’s commercial growth by originating, structuring, and closing large-scale distributed energy solutions, including solar PV, battery energy storage, linear generators, and microgrids, for enterprise and Fortune 500 industrial and data center clients.
This role requires a seasoned sales leader with a proven track record in managing complex, consultative sales cycles and delivering high-value renewable energy transactions. The Senior Business Development Director will own relationships with executive stakeholders, navigate complex procurement processes, and work closely with internal teams to deliver tailored solutions that meet customer goals.
The ideal candidate is a strategic, customer-focused dealmaker who thrives in high-stakes environments and consistently delivers results, while contributing insights that help refine Calibrant’s broader go-to-market strategy.
Principal Duties and Responsibilities
Business Development & Market Growth

- Originate and lead large-scale sales opportunities with Fortune 500 industrial and data center clients.

- Identify and target strategic accounts, positioning Calibrant’s solar, battery storage, linear generators, and microgrid solutions as enablers of sustainability, reliability, capacity, and cost optimization.

- Build trusted, consultative relationships with executive-level stakeholders.

- Stay ahead of energy transition trends, regulatory shifts, and customers’ needs to proactively identify opportunities.

Complex Sales & Transaction Leadership

- Manage the full sales cycle, from initial engagement through closing, with a focus on structuring and securing long-term agreements.

- Lead negotiations for PPAs, ESAs, and other complex contracts, ensuring terms meet client expectations while delivering company growth targets.

- Partner with engineering, project finance, and operations teams to build customized, bankable solutions.

- Maintain a disciplined and transparent pipeline, ensuring accurate forecasting and reporting.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Collaborate with solutions engineering, marketing, operations, and finance teams to align proposals with client needs.

- Support the preparation of investment committee materials and executive-level presentations for high-profile transactions.

- Provide market feedback to leadership to inform product strategy, pricing, and market positioning.

Performance & Growth Targets

- Consistently achieve or exceed annual sales and margin goals.

- Represent Calibrant at key client meetings, industry events, and conferences to expand visibility and strengthen brand presence.

- Build long-term partnerships with clients, ensuring repeat and expanded business opportunities.

Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Economics, or related field; MBA preferred.

- 7+ years of progressive experience in business development, commercial sales, or strategic partnerships within renewable energy, distributed generation, or energy infrastructure.

- Demonstrated success leading multi-million-dollar renewable energy transactions.

- Experience selling into Fortune 500 clients with ability to navigate complex organizational structures and procurement processes.

- Strong knowledge of solar PV, battery energy storage, linear generators, and microgrid systems.

- Proven ability to negotiate and close complex agreements (PPAs, ESAs, term sheets, LOIs).

- Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with ability to influence executive stakeholders.

- Self-driven, highly organized, and capable of managing multiple high-priority opportunities simultaneously.

- Willingness to travel up to 25% across North America.

Substantial commission opportunity in addition to base pay

title: Senior Electrical Engineer
description:
Calibrant Energy develops, owns, and operates on-site energy solutions for large power users. Working across distributed energy assets including solar, battery storage, and microgrids, the company helps customers advance practical, resilient solutions that support the energy transition. This is an opportunity to contribute to complex energy infrastructure projects in a business focused on technical rigor, operational performance, and long-term asset value.
As a Senior Electrical Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping the engineering quality and technical execution of distributed energy projects. You will work across internal and external stakeholders to support project development, design review, and asset performance, bringing strong electrical engineering judgment to systems that must meet demanding customer, utility, and operational requirements.
Responsibilities

- Lead electrical design and provide technical support across distributed energy projects.

- Review single-line diagrams, load flow studies, and interconnection packages.

- Collaborate with utilities, customers, and consultants on project engineering.

- Ensure designs meet electrical codes, standards, and project requirements.

- Support commissioning and operational troubleshooting for energy assets.

- Additional tasks as required.

Requirements
Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from an ABET-accredited program.

- At least 5 years of professional experience in the renewables and environment industry, focused on developing and implementing solutions that accelerate the energy transition.

- Hands-on experience with battery storage energy generation technologies and a proven ability to manage multiple projects.

- At least 5 years of experience working with utilities, customers, and external engineering partners.

- Strong knowledge of IEEE standards and NFPA-related electrical standards.

- Authorized to work in the United States.

- Able to travel to client sites as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with PV solar energy generation technologies.

- Background negotiating contracts and overseeing delivery schedules.

- Experience with power system modeling tools for load flow studies, as well as solar or storage design software and AutoCAD.

- Familiarity with energy efficiency measures.

- Experience managing consulting engineers and vendors.

- PE license.

title: Supply Chain Manager, Capital Equipment
description:
About Calibrant Energy
Calibrant is a leading provider of on-site energy solutions. Calibrant develops, owns, and operates large-scale solar, battery storage, and microgrids on behalf of our customers, empowering North America's largest power users to achieve their energy goals faster, more economically, and more sustainably.
By combining innovative financing with deep industry expertise, we solve complex energy challenges for large organizations. Our performance-based, no-capex contracts ensure we only get paid when we deliver results, enabling organizations to share in cost savings without any upfront investment.
Position Overview
The Supply Chain Manager is responsible for developing and executing supply chain strategies for capital equipment supporting energy infrastructure projects including, battery energy storage systems (BESS), solar generation projects, other generation solutions, and related electrical infrastructure. This role manages the procurement lifecycle from supplier engagement, sourcing, evaluation, negotiations, purchase order execution, and supplier relationship management through project delivery support.
The position will serve as a key interface between Supply Chain, Project Development, Engineering, Construction, Asset Management, Finance, Legal, and external suppliers to ensure equipment availability, supplier capacity, and procurement commitments are aligned with Calibrant's project pipeline. This role will also own and maintain working tools that support pipeline and supply alignment, commodity tracking, equipment allocation, procurement visibility, and supply chain risk management.
Principal Duties and Responsibilities

- Develop and execute sourcing strategies for major capital equipment, including transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, inverters, solar modules, RMUs, and related electrical balance-of-plant equipment.

- Lead RFPs, RFQs, bid evaluations, supplier comparisons, commercial analysis, and award recommendations to Head of Supply Chain for assigned equipment categories and projects.

- Negotiate pricing, delivery schedules, payment terms, warranties, commercial terms, purchase order requirements, framework agreements, contract amendments, change orders, and related supplier documentation.

- Issue, manage, and track purchase orders and supplier commitments to support project schedules, internal approvals, and project execution requirements.

- Maintain alignment between project pipeline forecasts and supplier capacity, production slots, long-lead procurement requirements, and available equipment allocations.

- Manage supply chain working tools, including equipment allocation trackers, pipeline/supply alignment models, procurement schedules, commodity tracking files, inventory visibility tools, and supply chain risk registers.

- Track market trends and commodity drivers impacting transformers, switchgear, steel, copper, freight, tariffs, domestic content requirements, FEOC exposure, and other regulatory or supply market factors.

- Build and maintain strong supplier relationships with OEMs, manufacturers, logistics providers, and other strategic capital equipment suppliers.

- Monitor supplier performance against cost, quality, responsiveness, delivery, documentation, and commercial requirements.

- Coordinate cross-functionally with Engineering, Development, Construction, Legal, Finance, Asset Management, and senior leadership to ensure procurement decisions support project economics, timelines, and risk objectives.

- Prepare sourcing recommendations, project procurement updates, supplier updates, market intelligence summaries, procurement dashboards, and executive reporting materials.

- Identify supply chain risks and develop mitigation strategies, including supplier diversification, early procurement planning, alternate sourcing, capacity reservations, and contingency planning.

Requirements
Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Operations, Finance, or related field.

- 5-10+ years of experience in supply chain, procurement, strategic sourcing, commercial management, or capital equipment procurement.

- Experience procuring capital equipment for renewable energy, power generation, utility, EPC, infrastructure, manufacturing, or industrial projects.

- Demonstrated experience with purchase orders, supplier negotiations, commercial analysis, contract terms, and supplier relationship management.

- Experience negotiating directly with OEMs and manufacturers.

- Strong analytical skills with advanced proficiency in Excel and experience maintaining planning, forecasting, commodity tracking, or procurement management tools.

- Ability to work cross-functionally with technical, commercial, legal, finance, construction, and project execution teams.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present recommendations to senior leadership.

- Available to overlap with West Coast business hours.

- Experience with BESS, solar, microgrids, transformers, switchgear, or electrical infrastructure.

- Experience with ERP, procurement, inventory, project controls, or supply chain planning systems is preferred.

- MBA, CPSM, C.P.M., APICS, or similar procurement/supply chain certification preferred.

- Located on the West Coast of the United States is preferred but not essential.

We believe in fostering an inclusive environment in which employees feel encouraged to share their unique perspectives, leverage their strengths, and act authentically.
